column2: Pick over and wash the pulses; soak in plenty of water for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Discard the soaking water and rinse the pulses; this makes them easier to digest.
Bring the beans to the boil in fresh water and skim off the foam; parboil for 20 minutes and drain.
Dice the onion.
Add the beans and hot water; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook covered for 45–60 minutes until the beans crush easily between your fingers.
Add salt only after the pulses are soft; added early, the skins can toughen.
Remove from the heat and rest for 10 minutes so the texture settles.
Bring the chickpeas to the boil in fresh water and skim off the foam; parboil for 20 minutes and drain.
Add the chickpeas and hot water; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook covered for 50–70 minutes until the chickpeas are completely soft.
Pick over the lentils and wash several times until the water runs clear.
Parboil the lentils in boiling water for 10 minutes and drain.
Chop the onion finely and dice the carrot.
Heat the oil in the pan and sauté the onion and carrot for 4–5 minutes.
Add the lentils and water; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook with the lid ajar for 25–30 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Dice the onion, carrot and potato; grate the tomato.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and soften the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the carrot and potato and sauté for 5 minutes.
Rinse the cooked pulses in a colander and drain well.
Add the tomato, borlotti beans and water; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook covered for 25 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Remove from the heat and leave to cool; pilaki is served warm or cold.
Bring the lentils to the boil with 2.5 glasses of water; simmer over low heat, stirring now and then, for 20 minutes until they fall apart.
Remove from the heat, add the bulgur, stir and leave covered for 20 minutes.
Chop the onion finely; fry it in oil in a pan for 5 minutes, add the pepper paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the onion mixture to the lentils; once cool enough not to burn your hands, knead for 5 minutes.
Finely chop the spring onions; add them to the mixture with the lemon juice and a little salt and knead.
With wet hands, squeeze portions in your palm to make finger-marked patties.
Serve with lettuce leaves and lemon.
Dice the pepper small and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and a little salt in a small bowl.
Combine the black-eyed peas, pepper, spring onion and parsley in a large bowl.
Pour over the dressing and toss gently.
Add the chickpeas and spinach and stir until the spinach wilts.
Add the water; cook covered for 15–20 minutes until the spinach is tender.
Dice the tomato; chop the parsley finely.
Serve cold or at room temperature.
Boil the lentils in boiling water for 15–20 minutes, keeping them slightly firm; drain.
Add the hot water and salt; when it boils, lower the heat and cook covered for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Put a clean cloth under the lid and let it rest for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork.
Chop the onion finely; slice the courgettes into half-moons and grate the tomatoes.
Add the courgette and chickpeas and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water; cook covered for 20–25 minutes until the courgettes are tender.
Bring the lentils to the boil with the water; simmer over low heat, stirring now and then, for 20 minutes until they fall apart.
Chop the onion finely; fry it in oil in a pan for 5 minutes, add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the onion mixture to the lentils; once cooled a little, knead for 5 minutes.
With wet hands, squeeze portions in your palm to shape patties.
Because it contains cooked grain, don't leave it at room temperature for more than 2 hours; keep leftovers covered in the fridge for 2 days.
Parboil the lentils in boiling water for 15 minutes and drain.
Chop the onion finely and dice the carrot and potato.
Loosen the tomato paste with 2–3 spoonfuls of water in the pan and stir with the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, lentils and water; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook covered for 25–30 minutes until the lentils and vegetables are tender.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; lightly grease the tray.
In pregnancy, use cheese made from pasteurised milk.
Crumble the cheese and mix with finely chopped parsley.
Whisk the egg, milk and oil; set aside 2–3 spoonfuls for brushing the top.
Lay one sheet of yufka in the tray and moisten with the sauce; spread the second sheet in folds and moisten again.
Spread the cheese filling; cover with the last sheet in folds and moisten with sauce.
Brush the reserved sauce on top and cut into squares.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden on top and cooked through.
Cut a slice to check: the egg filling inside should be fully cooked with no wet parts.
Remove from the oven and rest for 10 minutes; it will slice more easily.
The milk should be just warm to the touch; hot milk kills the yeast.
Mix the warm milk, yeast and sugar and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Separate the egg: the white goes into the dough, the yolk is for brushing the top.
Add the flour, oil, egg white and a pinch of salt and knead for 8–10 minutes into a soft dough that doesn't stick to your hands.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 45 minutes until doubled.
Divide the dough into balls and roll into strips; twist or shape into rings and place on the tray.
Leave for 15 more minutes; meanwhile preheat the oven to 190°C.
Brush with egg yolk and bake for 20–25 minutes until golden.
Preheat the oven to 190°C; lightly grease the tray.
Wash the spinach in plenty of water and chop finely; cook in a pan for 3 minutes to evaporate the liquid, then cool.
Mix the spinach with the crumbled cheese.
Cut the yufka sheets in half; brush each piece with sauce, put filling along one edge and roll up.
Place the rolls seam side down on the greased tray.
Brush the remaining sauce on top and bake for 30–35 minutes until golden.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; line a tray with baking paper.
Crack the egg and set the yolk aside for brushing the top.
Add the egg white, yoghurt and oil and knead into a soft dough that doesn't stick to your hands; don't overwork it.
Crumble the cheese and mix with finely chopped dill.
Take walnut-sized pieces of dough and flatten them; put filling in the centre and seal.
Arrange on the tray and brush with egg yolk; bake for 20–25 minutes until golden on top.
Knead the flour, water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough that doesn't stick to your hands; cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Chop the onion finely and soften in oil for 4 minutes.
Mash the boiled potatoes and mix with the onion; season with salt.
Divide the dough into 4 balls and roll out thinly with a rolling pin.
Spread filling over one half, fold the other half over and press the edges.
Cook in a dry or very lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until golden.
Mix the flour, yeast and a pinch of salt; add the warm water and olive oil and knead for 8–10 minutes into a soft dough.
Chop the pitted olives and work them into the dough with the thyme.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 45 minutes until doubled.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces, shape into small loaves and arrange on a tray lined with baking paper.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the crusts are golden.
Tap the bottom of a loaf with your finger: if it sounds hollow, it is cooked inside.
Boil the lentils in boiling water for 12–15 minutes until soft; drain well and cool.
Finely grate the carrot and courgette and squeeze out the liquid firmly.
Mix the lentils, vegetables, egg, oat flour and a little salt; if soft, add 1 spoon of oat flour.
With wet hands shape walnut-sized patties and arrange them on the tray.
Brush the tops with oil and bake for 15 minutes.
Turn and bake for 8–10 more minutes until golden on both sides.
Chop the onion finely and crush the garlic; grate the tomatoes.
Heat the oil in a pan and soften the onion for 4 minutes; add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Mix the borlotti beans with the sauce and water in the ovenproof dish; season with salt.
Bake for about 25 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the cauliflower, chickpeas and water; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook covered for 20–25 minutes until the cauliflower is tender.
Slit the leeks lengthwise and wash the layers well; chop finely.
Soften the leek in half the oil in a pan for 8 minutes and let it cool.
Mix the cooled leek with the crumbled cheese.
Whisk the egg with the milk; set half aside for the sheets and half for brushing the top.
Cut the yufka sheets in half and moisten lightly with sauce; divide the filling and roll up.
Brush the remaining sauce on top and bake for 30 minutes until golden.
Mash the chickpeas with a fork or pulse briefly in a food processor; don't make a smooth purée.
Grate the onion and squeeze out the juice.
Knead the chickpeas, onion, egg, breadcrumbs, cumin and a little salt.
Chop the onion finely and dice the carrot; grate the tomatoes.
Heat the oil in the pan and soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes.
Cook with the lid ajar for 20–25 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Mix the yoghurt, egg white and oil; add the flour and baking powder gradually.
Fold in the crumbled cheese and finely chopped dill to make a soft dough that doesn't stick to your hands; don't overwork it.
Take walnut-sized pieces, roll into balls and arrange spaced apart on the tray.
Brush the tops with egg yolk.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until cooked through and golden on top.
Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the onion for 4 minutes; add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Mix the borlotti beans, sauce, hot water, thyme and a little salt in the ovenproof dish.
Bake for 25 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Wash and finely chop the spinach; cook in a pan for 3 minutes to evaporate the liquid, then cool.
Cut the yufka into triangles or strips and brush with sauce; add filling and roll into small rolls.
Brush the remaining sauce on top and bake for 25 minutes until golden.
Mash the borlotti beans with a fork.
Knead the borlotti beans, onion, egg, breadcrumbs and a little salt.
Grate the tomatoes, mix with a little salt and spoon over the patties.
Bake for 25 minutes until the patties firm up.
Boil and mash the potatoes.
Soften the leek in half the oil in a pan for 8 minutes.
Mix the leek and potato and season with a little salt; leave to cool.
Whisk the milk, egg and remaining oil.
Cut the yufka sheets in half and moisten with sauce; wrap the filling and roll up.
